ritonavir.t: Because of the potential for drug-drug interactions, use caution when prescribing Dutasteride to patients taking potent, chronic CYP3A4 enzyme inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir) [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)].
Use with caution in patients taking potent, chronic cytochrome P450 CYP3A4 enzyme inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir).

tamsulosin.t: The effect of administration of tamsulosin or terazosin on Dutasteride pharmacokinetic parameters has not been evaluated.
Coadministration of dutasteride and tamsulosin resulted in similar changes to serum PSA as dutasteride monotherapy.

digoxin.t: 7.5 Digoxin Dutasteride does not alter the steady-state pharmacokinetics of digoxin when administered concomitantly at a dose of 0.5 mg/day for 3 weeks [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)].

warfarin.t: 7.6 Warfarin Concomitant administration of Dutasteride 0.5 mg/day for 3 weeks with warfarin does not alter the steady-state pharmacokinetics of the S- or R-warfarin isomers or alter the effect of warfarin on prothrombin time [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)].

finasteride.t: In a 7-year placebo-controlled clinical trial with another 5 alpha-reductase inhibitor (finasteride 5 mg, PROSCAR), similar results for Gleason score 8-10 prostate cancer were observed (finasteride 1.8% versus placebo 1.1%).

cyp3a4_inh.t: The effect of potent CYP3A4 inhibitors on dutasteride has not been studied.

ccb.t: 7.3 Calcium Channel Antagonists Co administration of verapamil or diltiazem decreases dutasteride clearance and leads to increased exposure to Dutasteride.
